headline: A 2013 House bill that would have created a federal Energy Department program to secure supplies of key minerals like rare earth materials, but it was voted down in 2014.
what_it_does: The bill would have set up a Department of Energy research program to keep supplies of energy critical elements steady and secure. It would have told the President's science office to coordinate federal agencies on early warnings for shortages and on building a stable domestic supply chain. It would also have allowed federal loan guarantees for new technologies tied to certain rare earth material projects, and it would have repealed the National Critical Materials Act of 1984.

who_it_affects.group: Mining and materials companies working with rare earth and other critical elements
who_it_affects.how: They would have been able to seek federal loan guarantees for commercial projects using new or significantly improved technologies.

who_it_affects.group: Students and universities doing materials science research
who_it_affects.how: The Energy Department would have been directed to encourage multidisciplinary research collaborations and学生 opportunities at colleges and universities.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies with materials research duties
who_it_affects.how: Some duties of the Defense and Interior Secretaries would have been repealed, and coordination would have shifted to the President's science office and the National Science and Technology Council.
